title: RS256 algorithm with string secret causes runtime InvalidKeyError
description: `auth.py` sets `ALGORITHM = SecurityConfig.JWT_ALGORITHM` which defaults to `"RS256"` via env, then calls `jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)` where `SECRET_KEY` is a plain string from `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`. The `python-jose` library raises `InvalidKeyError: Could not deserialize key data` when RS256 is used with a string key — RSA requires actual RSA key objects. Every POST /api/v1/auth/token and /register will fail unless `JWT_ALGORITHM=HS256` is set in env.
recommendation: Switch `auth.py` to use `get_jwt_manager()` (already imported at line 15) for token creation/validation, or add env guard: if ALGORITHM != "HS256", load RSA key from env/secrets-manager rather than using JWT_SECRET_KEY string.
acceptance_test_hint: `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with valid credentials returns 200 (not 500); `pytest tests/test_auth.py::test_login` passes

title: V1DeprecationMiddleware treats all current /api/v1/ routes as deprecated — log spam and incorrect headers
description: `V1DeprecationMiddleware.dispatch()` at line 756 triggers `_handle_v1_request` for any path containing `/api/v1/`. Since all production routes now use `/api/v1/` as their versioned prefix, every request hits the deprecation handler, emitting `logger.warning("V1 API request … V1 is SUNSET")` and adding `Warning`, `Sunset`, `Deprecation`, `X-API-Status: sunset` headers to every response. Clients receive misleading sunset headers on all API calls.
recommendation: The V1DeprecationMiddleware was designed to intercept legacy `/api/v1/` calls from external clients migrating from an old API. Now that `/api/v1/` IS the current stable prefix, either (a) remove the middleware, (b) update it to only block specific old path patterns that no longer exist (e.g. `/api/v1/stock/{symbol}` without the 's'), or (c) rename current routes to `/api/v2/`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: no `Warning` or `Sunset` header on `GET /api/v1/stocks`; log level drops to DEBUG for normal requests

The alert endpoint also accepts free-form `alert_type` and `message` parameters with no validation.

title: aiohttp ClientSession closed before WebSocket can be used
description: `connect()` does `async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session: self.websocket = await session.ws_connect(...); ... self._receive_task = asyncio.create_task(self._receive_loop())` and then returns. The function returns from inside the `async with` — Python immediately exits the context manager and `session.__aexit__` is called, which closes the session and (per aiohttp semantics) the websocket created from it. The receive loop runs once, gets `WSMsgType.CLOSED`, breaks, calls `_handle_connection_error`, and reconnects in an infinite loop. Real-time price streaming via Finnhub will never function.
recommendation: Promote `self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()` to an instance attribute initialised in `__init__`, and close it in `disconnect()`. Do not use `async with` for a long-lived session. Pattern: `self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(); self.websocket = await self._session.ws_connect(...)`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: integration test connects to a stub Finnhub websocket, sends one trade message, receives it via callback within 1 s without reconnect. `aiohttp.ClientSession` lifetime equals the `FinnhubWebSocketClient` lifetime.

title: Live endpoints surface `random.uniform()` / `random.randint()` data as real values
description: Multiple service methods that are wired to authenticated production endpoints return Python-`random` simulated values with no flag indicating mock data: `admin_service.get_system_health_data()` (CPU/mem/error rate), `admin_service.list_users()` (entire user list), `recommendation_service.run_backtest()` (entire backtest result), `recommendation_service.generate_performance_records()` (recommendation P&L), `recommendation_service.generate_alert_history()`, `portfolio_rebalancing.generate_performance_data_points()` (portfolio chart values), `socketio_service._stream_price_updates()` (live price feed broadcast to subscribers). For a SEC-regulated investment platform this is both a correctness bug and a compliance risk: the platform's own SEC disclosure (`recommendation_service.py:25-31`) warns about data freshness yet here it ships entirely fabricated values without any `mock=True` flag.
recommendation: Tag every fake-data method with a `_DEMO_DATA = True` constant or wrap with a feature flag (`if not settings.DEMO_MODE: raise NotImplementedError`); ensure the response includes `"data_source": "simulated"`. Better: replace with real implementations where feasible (cleanup_old_data tasks already populate metrics; system metrics already collected by `monitoring`/`metrics` endpoints). At minimum, audit each call site and either implement or block with `HTTP 501 Not Implemented`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -nE "random\.(uniform | randint | choice)" backend/services/*.py` returns 0 hits in production code paths; demo-only code is gated behind `settings.DEMO_MODE`. Integration test on `/api/admin/system/health` returns `psutil`-based real numbers, not `random.uniform(20, 80)`.

Option (a) is preferred — the dual-system creates ambiguity.

title: `get_bulk_price_history` called with timezone-naive `datetime.now().date()`

description: Two services each define `_mem_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[float, object]]`, `_*_cache_get`, `_*_cache_set`, with TTL only differing (900 s vs 60 s). Identical patterns, no shared util. Fragile under multi-process Celery (each worker has its own dict; cache misses depending on which worker handles request).
recommendation: Extract to `backend/utils/local_ttl_cache.py` (or use existing `backend/utils/cache.py::LRUCache`). Both services import it.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -rn "_mem_cache\ | _price_cache" backend/services/` returns 0 hits; both services import from utils.

title: Two competing real-time push transports (raw WebSocket + Socket.IO)
description: `websocket_service.py::EnhancedConnectionManager` (active per scope-01 audit; `EnhancedConnectionManager` imported by `backend/api/routers/websocket.py:25-32`). `socketio_service.py::sio` is a Socket.IO `AsyncServer` instance with its own subscription model. Both broadcast price updates with mock data; clients must choose one. Dual code path with no integration plan.
recommendation: Pick one. Socket.IO is friendlier for browsers behind proxies; raw WebSocket has lower overhead. Document the choice in `docs/architecture/` and delete the other. The `_stream_price_updates` random-data emitter in socketio_service exists in BOTH transports (F-02-003) — fixing one without the other still ships fake data.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: only one transport is registered in `main.py`; frontend WebSocket client code points to one URL.

title: `day_change` calculation uses heuristic `* 0.01` magic number
description: `day_change += position.quantity * (price_update.close - position.average_cost) * 0.01`. The 0.01 multiplier is unexplained — it converts the gain-vs-cost into an approximate daily change but the math is incorrect (close - average_cost is total gain since entry, not day change). The day_change passed to clients is a hand-tuned guess.
recommendation: Use `price_update.change` (per-share daily change) directly: `day_change += position.quantity * price_update.change`. The `RealtimePriceService` already returns `change` field (see `realtime_price_service.py:42`).
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: integration test with known prices verifies `day_change` matches `Σ qty × per-share-change`.

title: `calculate_rsi` and `calculate_macd` are stub `return None`
description: Despite their bodies being a single `return None`, both are exported from the module and may be imported by tests. They are misleading — the file has helper logic for fetching real RSI/MACD via `alpha_vantage_client.get_rsi(...)` (lines 116-127) but the local stubs invite callers to use the broken pure-Python version.

acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -nE "def calculate_(rsi\ | macd)" backend/services/analysis_service.py` returns 0 hits OR functions return real values for sample inputs.

title: Fallback risk metrics return hardcoded plausible-but-fake values
description: When `prices` is short or empty, returns `{"beta": 1.15, "alpha": 0.02, "sharpe_ratio": 1.85, ...}`. These look like real risk metrics. A caller that doesn't check `len(prices) >= 30` upstream will surface them to the user as "risk metrics for [TICKER] with no data". Same problem as F-02-003 (silent fake data).
recommendation: Return `{}` or raise `InsufficientDataError`. Caller should explicitly handle the missing-data case.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `if prices and len(prices) >= 30` short-path returns real metrics; else raises explicit exception.

title: Investment Thesis feature has no service layer
description: `INVESTMENT_THESIS_FEATURE.md` documents a service layer between router and repo, but `ls backend/services/` shows no `thesis_service.py`. The router (scope 01) likely calls `thesis_repository` directly, bypassing the layered architecture documented in `services/__init__.py:1-3`.

acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `backend/services/thesis_service.py` exists OR architecture doc declares the exception explicitly.

title: No tests for the broken-by-design `connect()` flow
description: F-02-002 is a 2-hour fix but the bug has presumably shipped because no test exercises an end-to-end Finnhub WebSocket connect-and-receive cycle. `grep -rn "FinnhubWebSocketClient\
recommendation: realtime_price_service" backend/tests/` to confirm.

title: `create_socketio_asgi_app` not invoked in main.py
description: The function is exported and documented but `grep -rn "create_socketio_asgi_app" backend/` returns 1 hit (the definition). `main.py` does not mount the Socket.IO app at the top level. Either Socket.IO is intentionally disabled (then delete the file) or main.py forgot the integration step.

title: Sector approximation uses `pos.symbol[:2]`
description: `unique_sectors = len(set(pos.symbol[:2] for pos in positions))` uses the first 2 chars of the ticker as a sector proxy. This bears no relation to actual sector and produces nonsense (e.g., AAPL and AAL both `AA`; MSFT and META don't match). The diversification bonus computed from this is meaningless.
recommendation: Read `pos.stock.sector` (already available via repo). If positions are domain models without `sector`, look up via `stock_repository.get_by_symbols_bulk(...)` (combine with F-02-007).
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `unique_sectors` matches the count of distinct `Stock.sector` values for the position list.

title: Module-level engine singletons not thread-safe
description: `_fundamental_engine`, `_technical_engine`, `_sentiment_engine` use `global` and a None-check. In a multi-thread test runner or under FastAPI's threadpool fallback, two requests racing the lazy init can each construct a separate engine.
recommendation: Wrap with `asyncio.Lock` or use `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)`. Or instantiate at module import time.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: concurrent-stress test does not produce two engine instances.

title: Two scheduling systems both documented as canonical
description: Module docstring of `scheduler.py` says "Async Task Scheduler for background operations". `celery_app.py` configures full Celery beat. Operators don't know which one to run.
recommendation: Document in `docs/architecture/` which is canonical (Celery beat) and demote `scheduler.py` to a dev-only fallback or delete (per F-02-004).
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: docs/architecture has clear answer.

title: Symbol validation uses `isalpha() or len(symbol) > 5`
description: Inline regex-equivalent logic instead of using `backend/utils/validation.py::InputValidator.PATTERNS["ticker"]` (cited in scope 11 audit, F-11 evidence row). Each service rolls its own ticker validation.
recommendation: Import the canonical validator.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -n "isalpha\ | symbol\.isalnum" backend/services/` shows shared validator usage instead of inline checks.

title: Unauthenticated model management endpoints
description: `POST /models/{name}/load`, `DELETE /models/{name}`, and `POST /retrain` have no authentication. Server binds `0.0.0.0` with `allow_origins=["*"]`. Any network peer can unload production models or trigger compute-intensive retraining.
recommendation: Add API key or JWT auth to all mutating endpoints using FastAPI `Depends`. Restrict CORS origins to known frontend domains. Consider binding to `127.0.0.1` or behind an internal reverse proxy.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8001/models/lstm_price_predictor` should return 401 without auth header

title: `torch.load()` without `weights_only=True` — arbitrary code execution risk
description: Five `torch.load()` calls across `model_manager.py:221,300`, `model_versioning.py:594`, `artifact_manager.py:180`, `training/evaluate_models.py:91` omit `weights_only=True`. PyTorch 2.0+ warns this allows arbitrary pickle execution when loading untrusted `.pth` files.
recommendation: Add `weights_only=True` to all `torch.load()` calls. For full model objects use `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals()` pattern.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "torch.load" backend/ml/ | grep -v weights_only` returns no results

title: Trained model binaries absent — platform runs on dummy fallbacks
description: `ml_models/` contains only JSON config/result files. No `xgboost_model.pkl`, `lstm_weights.pth`, or Prophet `.pkl` files exist. `model_manager.py:199-211` silently substitutes `DummyLSTM`, `DummyXGBoost`, `DummyProphet` that return random values. All ML-driven recommendations in production are random-based, not model-based.
recommendation: Run full training pipeline to produce and store model binaries, or download from HF Hub (`HF_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true`). Add startup health gate that fails fast if all models are in fallback state.
acceptance_test_hint: `ls ml_models/*.pkl ml_models/*.pth` lists files; `GET /health` returns `fallback_models: 0`

title: XGBoost model R²=−0.011, all feature importances zero
description: `evaluation_report.json` reports R²=−0.011 (worse than predicting the mean) and direction_accuracy=46.5% (below coin flip). `xgboost_training_results.json` shows all 57 feature importances as 0.0 — the model learned nothing. This suggests a data pipeline bug (e.g., target leakage, improper scaling, or empty training split).
recommendation: Audit training data pipeline: verify target variable construction, check train/test split for look-ahead bias, ensure feature values are non-zero before training. Add assertion `r2 > 0.0` as model acceptance gate.
acceptance_test_hint: `python -m backend.ml.training.evaluate_models` reports `r2 > 0.0` and at least one non-zero feature importance

title: Feature drift monitoring and statistics use mock random data
description: `monitor_feature_drift()` at line 666 reads: `"Mock data for demonstration - in real implementation, query feature store"` and generates `np.random.normal(0,1,1000)`. `get_feature_statistics()` at line 743 returns `np.random.randint(1000, 10000)` for counts and other random values. Drift alerts will fire randomly regardless of actual data distribution.
recommendation: Implement real feature store persistence using the SQLAlchemy `db_engine` already initialized in `__init__`. Query actual feature values from DB or time-series storage for drift calculation.
acceptance_test_hint: `monitor_feature_drift("rsi_14d")` returns a `FeatureDriftMetrics` whose `drift_score` changes with actual data, not randomly

title: Path traversal in model name parameter — arbitrary file load
description: `load_model(model_name)` constructs `Path(f"backend/ml_models/{model_name}.pkl")` with no validation. An attacker can pass `model_name="../../../etc/passwd"` via `POST /models/../../../etc/passwd/load` to attempt loading arbitrary files via joblib, or enumerate paths.
recommendation: Validate `model_name` against `re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", model_name)` before path construction. Use `Path.resolve()` and assert the resolved path is within `models_path`.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/models/../../../etc/passwd/load` returns 400, not 500

title: Hardcoded relative path in FileHandler — fails when CWD is not project root
description: `logging.FileHandler(f'backend/ml_logs/training_{...}.log')` uses a relative path. When the script is run from any directory other than the project root (e.g., from `/app` in Docker or from `backend/`), the log directory will not be found and training will fail silently or crash. `simple_training_pipeline.py:26` has the same issue.
recommendation: Replace relative path with `Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "ml_logs" / f"training_{...}.log"` or use `os.getenv("ML_LOGS_PATH")`.
acceptance_test_hint: Training pipeline runs from any working directory and produces log files at the correct absolute path

title: Feature store builtin coverage is much narrower than documented
description: Documentation (`ML_PIPELINE_DOCUMENTATION.md`) claims the feature store manages "MACD, Bollinger Bands, sentiment features, volatility, volume patterns, correlation metrics." The `builtin_features` dict at `feature_store.py:341-353` only implements: `price_return_1d`, `price_return_5d`, `price_volatility_20d`, `volume_ratio_20d`, `rsi_14d`, `sma_20d`, `ema_20d`, `pe_ratio`, `market_cap` (9 features). MACD, Bollinger Bands, and sentiment are absent.
recommendation: Implement missing technical indicators or update documentation to reflect actual scope. Add `_compute_macd()`, `_compute_bollinger_bands()` methods and register them.
acceptance_test_hint: Feature store `builtin_features` dict contains at minimum MACD and Bollinger Band compute functions

title: Bare `except:` in predict endpoint silences all errors
description: `confidence` calculation at `ml_api_server.py:175-178` uses bare `except: pass` — this swallows any exception including `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, and `SystemExit`. Should be `except Exception:` at minimum.
recommendation: Replace bare `except:` with `except Exception as e: logger.debug(f"proba unavailable: {e}")`
acceptance_test_hint: `pylint backend/ml/ml_api_server.py` reports no bare-except violations

title: `OnlineLearner.update()` raises `NotImplementedError`
description: `online_learning.py:103` — `raise NotImplementedError` in the base `OnlineLearner.update()` method. Subclasses `IncrementalLearner` and `SGDIncrementalLearner` exist but the online learning system has no integration with the main inference path (`model_manager.py` or `ml_api_server.py`). The system is architecturally isolated.

title: Duplicate simplified pipeline is dead code
description: `simple_training_pipeline.py` (`"Phase 4 Testing"`) duplicates functionality of `training_pipeline.py` without being integrated into any production path. It provides its own `SimpleMLTrainingPipeline` class with the same `_load_config()` / `initialize()` flow. No import of this module found in any other file outside tests.

title: Feature computation iterates entities in a Python `for` loop — O(N×M)
description: `_compute_single_feature()` and all `_compute_*` built-ins iterate `entity_ids` one-by-one with Python loops rather than vectorized pandas operations. For 6,000 stocks, this creates 6,000 row-filter operations per feature per compute call.
recommendation: Refactor built-in feature computations to use grouped pandas operations: `price_data.groupby("ticker")["close"].last()` instead of per-ticker loops.
acceptance_test_hint: Feature computation for 6,000 tickers and 9 built-in features completes in <5 seconds on CPU

title: Operations guide references wrong model file path
description: Guide instructs `df -h backend/ml_models/` but model files are at `ml_models/` (project root) and the path `backend/ml_models/` does not exist. Same drift in `ML_QUICKSTART.md` which refers to `backend/ml_models/`.
recommendation: Update all documentation to use `ml_models/` (project root path) consistently.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "backend/ml_models" docs/ml/` returns no results

title: No integration tests for the ML API server endpoints
description: Test files `test_ml_pipeline.py` and `test_ml_performance.py` use mocks and unit-level tests. No tests exercise the live FastAPI `ml_api_server.py` via `TestClient`. Security-sensitive endpoints (`/retrain`, `/models/{name}/load`, `DELETE`) have zero test coverage.
recommendation: Add `TestClient(app)` integration tests for all CRUD endpoints in `ml_api_server.py`, including negative cases for path traversal and unauthenticated access.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_ml_api_server.py` passes with ≥80% endpoint coverage

title: `_load_pytorch_model` is defined but never called
description: `model_manager.py:218-226` defines `_load_pytorch_model()` which calls `torch.load(path)` directly. The actual LSTM loader `_load_lstm_model()` at line 250 uses its own `torch.load()` inline. The standalone method is dead code.
recommendation: Remove `_load_pytorch_model()` or refactor LSTM loader to call it (after adding `weights_only=True`).
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "_load_pytorch_model" backend/ml/model_manager.py` shows only definition, no call sites

title: Rate limiting documented but not implemented
description: Document claims "1000 requests/minute per client" and "Burst: up to 50 requests in 10 seconds" with rate-limit headers. No rate limiting middleware (`slowapi`, `limits`, or custom) exists in `ml_api_server.py`.
recommendation: Either implement rate limiting (e.g., `slowapi`) or remove the rate limiting section from the docs.
acceptance_test_hint: `ml_api_server.py` imports `slowapi` and attaches limiter, OR docs section removed

title: MD5 used for cache key generation
description: `_generate_cache_key()` at line 764 uses `hashlib.md5()`. MD5 has known collision vulnerabilities. While not a security-critical use here (cache key only, no authentication), better_pattern is to use `hashlib.sha256()` or `hashlib.blake2b()` for consistency with any future security-sensitive hash usage.
recommendation: Replace `hashlib.md5` with `hashlib.sha256` in cache key generation.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "hashlib.md5" backend/ml/feature_store.py` returns no results

title: Hardcoded developer absolute path for `data_dir`
description: `"data_dir": "/Users/yluo/Documents/Code/ScAI/FR1-data"` is a personal machine path. Any deployment other than the original developer's laptop will silently produce empty results or raise `FileNotFoundError` on all offline data tools.
recommendation: Replace with `os.getenv("TRADINGAGENTS_DATA_DIR", str(Path.home() / "tradingagents-data"))` or a project-relative fallback; document env var in README.
acceptance_test_hint: `assert os.path.isabs(DEFAULT_CONFIG["data_dir"])` passes and path is derived from env var in a fresh env without that filesystem path.

title: `fundamentals_report` variable assigned `news_report` value
description: Line 14: `fundamentals_report = state["news_report"]` — the fundamentals report is never read; instead the news report is passed twice into the LLM context string on line 18. The Risk Manager therefore cannot reason about fundamentals data at all.
recommendation: Change line 14 to `fundamentals_report = state["fundamentals_report"]`.

title: File handle leak in `get_data_in_range`
description: `data = open(data_path, "r")` is never closed. In a backtest loop over many dates/tickers this will exhaust the OS file descriptor limit and raise `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files`.
recommendation: Replace with `with open(data_path, "r") as f: data = json.load(f)` and remove the separate `json.load(data)` call.
acceptance_test_hint: Pytest with `mock_open` verifies `__exit__` is called; OS-level FD count does not grow during a 100-iteration loop.

title: `FinancialSituationMemory` uses OpenAI client for embeddings regardless of provider
description: The constructor creates `self.client = OpenAI(base_url=config["backend_url"])` and always calls `client.embeddings.create`. For Anthropic or Google providers the base URL is incompatible; the embedding call will fail with an HTTP error, causing `reflect_and_remember` to raise at runtime.
recommendation: Gate embedding client on provider: use OpenAI client only for OpenAI/Ollama/OpenRouter; skip embeddings or raise a clear `NotImplementedError` for unsupported providers. Long-term, use `langchain_community` embeddings that match the provider.
acceptance_test_hint: Integration test with `llm_provider="anthropic"` config does not crash on `reflect_and_remember`.

title: OpenAI `responses.create` API call stores conversation data server-side (`store=True`)
description: `get_stock_news_openai`, `get_global_news_openai`, and `get_fundamentals_openai` all pass `store=True` to `client.responses.create`. This persists potentially sensitive ticker/date queries in OpenAI's servers, which may violate data residency or compliance requirements for a financial platform.
recommendation: Set `store=False` unless explicit user opt-in; add a config key `openai_store_responses` defaulting to `False`.
acceptance_test_hint: Config-driven test asserts `store` kwarg value matches config setting.

title: LLM provider branch uses `ChatOpenAI` for Ollama/OpenRouter without appropriate headers
description: The `ollama` and `openrouter` providers are handled via `ChatOpenAI` pointing at a custom `backend_url`, but OpenRouter requires `x-title` and `HTTP-Referer` headers that `ChatOpenAI` does not add by default. Ollama may need `num_ctx` model param. Silent degradation or auth errors will occur at runtime.
recommendation: Add provider-specific configuration: for OpenRouter pass `default_headers` to `ChatOpenAI`; for Ollama pass `model_kwargs`. Add a `"openrouter"` explicit branch or document limitations.
acceptance_test_hint: CLI integration test with mocked OpenRouter endpoint asserts required headers are present.

title: Wildcard `from tradingagents.agents import *` used in critical graph wiring
description: `setup.py:8`, `trading_graph.py:15`, `agent_states.py:5` all use `from tradingagents.agents import *`. This makes the import surface implicit, prevents static analysis tools from resolving names, and means any future accidental `__all__` change breaks graph compilation silently.
recommendation: Replace star imports with explicit imports of the symbols actually used (`create_market_analyst`, `GraphSetup`, etc.).
acceptance_test_hint: `mypy --strict` on `graph/setup.py` reports no "Name not defined" errors.

title: `trader_node` signature takes `name` as positional but `functools.partial` passes it as keyword
description: `trader_node(state, name)` is called via `functools.partial(trader_node, name="Trader")`. LangGraph calls nodes with a single positional argument `(state,)`. The partial wrapping means `name` will never be passed correctly by LangGraph's node invocation, so `name` will always be the partial-captured `"Trader"` string — which is the intended behavior, but the function signature is misleading and fragile. Additionally, `sender` is set in the return dict but not declared in `AgentState`.
recommendation: Refactor to a closure like the other agent factories; remove the `functools.partial` pattern. Declare `sender` in `AgentState` or remove the key from the return dict.
acceptance_test_hint: `AgentState.__annotations__` contains `sender`; mypy passes on trader.py.

title: `setup.py` pins stale/missing package versions; no `langchain-anthropic` or `langchain-google-genai`
description: `setup.py` installs `langchain-openai>=0.0.2` (current is `>=0.1`) and lists `langchain>=0.1.0` but does NOT include `langchain-anthropic` or `langchain-google-genai`, which are imported unconditionally in `trading_graph.py:11-12`. Installing via `pip install tradingagents` and using Anthropic/Google providers will fail with `ImportError`.
recommendation: Add `langchain-anthropic>=0.1.0` and `langchain-google-genai>=1.0.0` to `install_requires`; pin `langchain-openai>=0.1.0`.
acceptance_test_hint: Fresh virtualenv install; `python -c "from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph"` succeeds without extra manual installs.

title: Typo in docstring: "Makrdown"
description: Line 21: `" Make sure to append a Makrdown table..."` — typo "Makrdown". Minor but propagated to LLM system prompt, which affects model instruction quality.

acceptance_test_hint: String search confirms "Makrdown" absent.

title: `system_message` is assigned as a tuple, not a string
description: Line 24-26: `system_message = ("You are a researcher...", )` — trailing comma makes this a 1-element tuple. The prompt partial receives a tuple, not a string. LangChain will silently coerce it but the behavior is undefined and causes unexpected whitespace/formatting in the system message.
recommendation: Remove the trailing comma on line 26: `system_message = ("You are a researcher..." + " Make sure...")` → `system_message = "You are a researcher..." + " Make sure..."`.
acceptance_test_hint: `isinstance(system_message, str)` is true at runtime.

title: Filename typo: `aggresive_debator.py` (missing 'r' in aggressive)
description: File `aggresive_debator.py` should be `aggressive_debator.py`. The misspelling is also in `__init__.py:13` (`from .risk_mgmt.aggresive_debator import create_risky_debator`).
recommendation: Rename file to `aggressive_debator.py` and update import in `__init__.py`.
acceptance_test_hint: `find backend/TradingAgents -name "aggresive_debator.py"` returns no results.

title: `get_stock_stats_indicators_window` offline mode iterates day-by-day calling `get_stockstats_indicator` per day
description: Lines 526-535: for each day in `look_back_days`, a full stockstats DataFrame is re-computed (re-reading the CSV, wrapping, computing the indicator column) for a single row lookup. For 30-day windows this triggers 30 independent CSV reads and `stockstats.wrap` calls.

title: `get_reddit_global_news` uses a tqdm progress bar in a server-side call

acceptance_test_hint: Server-side call with `show_progress=False` produces no stderr output.

title: `Toolkit._config` is a class-level mutable dict shared across all instances
description: `_config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()` at class level means all `Toolkit` instances share state. Calling `Toolkit.update_config(...)` on one instance mutates the config seen by all other instances in the same process (e.g., in parallel or sequential backtests).
recommendation: Convert `_config` to an instance attribute in `__init__`; remove `update_config` classmethod, make it an instance method.
acceptance_test_hint: Two `Toolkit(config_a)` and `Toolkit(config_b)` instances have independent configs.

title: No tests for `FinancialSituationMemory`, `Toolkit`, or any analyst node
description: `test_trading_agents.py` covers `ConditionalLogic`, `Propagator`, `SignalProcessor`, `Reflector`, `AgentState`, `default_config`, and `dataflow/utils` — but has no tests for `FinancialSituationMemory.add_situations`, `get_memories`, any of the four analyst nodes, the researcher nodes, the trader node, or the risk debators. Memory and analyst logic are the highest-value components.
recommendation: Add mocked tests for `FinancialSituationMemory` (mock chromadb client), analyst node creation (mock LLM), and trader node.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_trading_agents.py -v` shows coverage >80% for `memory.py` and `analysts/`.

title: `_log_state` writes to relative path `eval_results/`
description: Line 225-232: `Path(f"eval_results/{self.ticker}/...")` is relative to whatever the current working directory is at invocation time. When called from inside the platform's backend service, the log files will be written to an unpredictable location.

title: `asyncio.new_event_loop` / `set_event_loop` is an anti-pattern in Python 3.10+
description: `run_etl_pipeline` and `run_incremental_update` use `asyncio.new_event_loop()` + `asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)` then `loop.run_until_complete(...)`. On Python 3.10+ the preferred idiom is `asyncio.run(coro)`, which handles loop creation and cleanup correctly, avoids event loop leaks if an exception occurs before `loop.close()`, and does not pollute the thread's event loop slot.

title: `transaction()` context manager is silently broken

Awaiting an async generator call returns the generator object; the body (including `yield session`) never executes. Every caller of `repo.transaction()` receives no session and silently does nothing.
recommendation: Rewrite `_execute_transaction` as a plain `async def` returning a result, or use `asynccontextmanager` correctly by restructuring so the retry loop wraps the async context manager. Alternatively, refactor `transaction()` to use `db_manager.get_session()` directly.

PostgreSQL does not support this syntax — MySQL does. The entire table creation will fail with a parse error.

title: Exchange/Sector/Industry→Stock relationships use `lazy="selectin"` globally
description: `Exchange.stocks`, `Sector.stocks`, `Sector.industries`, and `Industry.stocks` are all defined with `lazy="selectin"`. Any query fetching a single `Exchange`, `Sector`, or `Industry` row will immediately issue additional SELECT queries loading every associated `Stock` record — potentially thousands per lookup. This pattern was chosen to prevent `MissingGreenlet` in async context, but applies even when stock data is not needed.
recommendation: Change these reverse collection relationships to `lazy="select"` (lazy load on attribute access) or `lazy="raise"` (raise if accidentally accessed) and rely on `selectinload()` in queries that genuinely need the stock list. Alternatively use `lazy="noload"` and explicitly opt-in.

title: `Position` ORM model missing `version` column added by migration
description: `add_row_locking_versions.sql` adds `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` to the `positions` table (line 17). The `Position` class in `unified_models.py` has no `version` column (confirmed: lines 664–706 show no such column). Reads from `positions` after migration runs will have a DB column not reflected in the ORM, causing SQLAlchemy to silently ignore it. Optimistic locking for positions is thus non-functional despite being documented.
recommendation: Add `version = Column(Integer, default=1, nullable=False, server_default='1')` to the `Position` model. Create an Alembic migration to align the ORM with the existing SQL migration.
acceptance_test_hint: `position.version` returns an integer; `update_with_lock` on a `Position` increments version correctly.

title: ML training code misplaced in `backend/models/`

title: Mutable `dict`/`list` literals used as SQLAlchemy `Column` defaults
description: `Column(JSON, default={})` at lines 102, 967, 1128 and `Column(JSON, default=["email"])` at line 842. SQLAlchemy evaluates the `default` expression once at class definition time. All rows created without an explicit value share the same dict/list object — mutation of one row's JSON field can corrupt another in-memory until flushed.
recommendation: Replace with `default=dict` (callable) or `default=list` respectively. For dicts with initial values use a lambda: `default=lambda: {"email_daily_summary": True, ...}`.

title: `UserSession` missing index on `expires_at` column

title: `update()` unconditionally strips `None` values, preventing intentional NULL updates
description: `update_data = {k: v for k, v in update_data.items() if v is not None}` at lines 349 and 427 removes all `None` values before the UPDATE. Callers can never set a nullable column to NULL via the standard `update()` method (e.g., clearing `User.locked_until`, `Stock.ipo_date`).

title: Migration 002 `try/except` silently swallows TimescaleDB failures with no warning

There is no log message, no status column, and no validation at end of migration.
recommendation: At minimum, log a warning when the TimescaleDB path is skipped: `logger.warning("TimescaleDB not available; falling back to manual partitioning")`. Add a post-migration validation query to verify the chosen path succeeded.

title: `synchronous_commit = off` trades durability for throughput without documentation
description: `synchronous_commit = off` means PostgreSQL acknowledges commits before WAL records are flushed to disk. Up to ~200ms of committed transactions can be lost on a power failure. For an investment platform storing transaction records and portfolio positions, this is an unacceptable durability trade-off with no inline justification or per-table override strategy.
recommendation: Document the explicit risk decision inline. For tables storing financial transactions (`transactions`, `orders`, `positions`) consider `synchronous_commit = on` at the session level (SET LOCAL synchronous_commit = on) within those write paths.
acceptance_test_hint: `SHOW synchronous_commit` on a session writing to `transactions` returns `on` (or the risk decision is explicitly documented and signed off).

title: `_calculate_obv` and `_calculate_ad_line` use Python loops over numpy arrays

title: Custom registry isolation hides all SLA, health, and alerting Prometheus metrics
description: `metrics_collector.py` creates a private `CollectorRegistry` (line 35) and `generate_latest(registry)` (line 658) serves only that registry at `/metrics`. All metrics in `health_checks.py`, `alerting_system.py`, `application_monitoring.py`, `financial_monitoring.py`, and `database_performance.py` register to the **default** Prometheus registry (no `registry=` argument passed). `generate_latest()` (no args) for the default registry is never called. Result: Prometheus scrapes `/metrics` and gets only system/API/cost metrics — zero health-check, zero SLA compliance, zero alert metrics are exported.
recommendation: Unify all monitoring modules onto one registry. Either (a) pass the custom `registry` object to every `Gauge/Counter/Histogram` instantiation in all monitoring submodules, or (b) remove the custom registry from `metrics_collector.py` and call `generate_latest()` (no args) so all modules contribute to the default registry. Option (b) requires checking for name collisions first (see F-10-002).
acceptance_test_hint: `curl http://localhost:8000/metrics` returns text containing `health_check_status` and `sla_compliance_percent`; Prometheus target shows no missing series for health alerts.

title: `MimeText`/`MimeMultipart` import typo — email alerts silently fail at module load
description: Line 25: `from email.mime.text import MimeText` and line 26: `from email.mime.multipart import MimeMultipart`. The stdlib classes are `MIMEText` and `MIMEMultipart` (all-caps MIME prefix). Python raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'MimeText'` on any import of this module. Lines 409 and 420 also reference `MimeMultipart()` and `MimeText(html_body, 'html')` using the incorrect names. Since `__init__.py` imports `alertmanager_webhook` (not `real_time_alerts`) the module may not fail at startup unless imported elsewhere, but all email alert delivery paths are broken.
recommendation: Change line 25 to `from email.mime.text import MIMEText`, line 26 to `from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart`, line 409 to `msg = MIMEMultipart()`, and line 420 to `msg.attach(MIMEText(html_body, 'html'))`.
acceptance_test_hint: `python -c "from backend.monitoring.real_time_alerts import AlertSeverity"` exits 0 with no ImportError; integration test sends a test alert email.

Gauges `data_quality_score`, `data_missing_percent`, and `data_staleness` are never populated.

acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "def get_quality_summary" backend/monitoring/data_quality_metrics.py` returns a hit; `data_quality_score` gauge has non-zero values in Prometheus after one collection cycle.

Simultaneously wire `backend/utils/monitoring.py` metrics to the served endpoint (see F-10-001) to resolve the dual-registry issue.

title: Counter internal `_value._value` mutated directly — breaks Prometheus atomicity guarantees
description: Lines 296-297: `network_bytes_sent.labels(interface='total')._value._value = net_io.bytes_sent` and `network_bytes_received.labels(interface='total')._value._value = net_io.bytes_recv`. This accesses the private internal attribute of a `Counter` object, bypassing the thread-safe increment API. Counters must be monotonically increasing; direct assignment can make the counter go backwards (e.g., if `net_io_counters()` resets after a reboot), violating Prometheus data model. Also breaks with any Prometheus client library version upgrade.
recommendation: Counters of cumulative OS bytes should use a `Gauge` not a `Counter` (or use `REGISTRY` provided by node-exporter instead). Replace with `Gauge('network_bytes_sent_total', ...)` and call `.set(net_io.bytes_sent)`. Or remove and rely on node-exporter's `node_network_transmit_bytes_total`.
acceptance_test_hint: `network_bytes_sent_total` (renamed to Gauge) has monotonically non-decreasing values over multiple scrapes; no `_value._value` references remain in metrics_collector.

title: Error budget recording rule uses 6-hour window — cannot represent 30-day monthly budget
description: `slo:error_budget_remaining:ratio` (line 187) is derived from `slo:api_availability:ratio_rate6h`, a 6-hour rolling average. The comment at line 4 states the error budget is "~43 min/month downtime." Using a 6-hour window means: (a) the budget resets every 6 hours, so sustained low-level degradation never exhausts it; (b) a 1-hour outage looks catastrophic on the 6h window but "recovers" as soon as the window rolls past. `SLOErrorBudgetLow` and `SLOErrorBudgetExhausted` will not fire under gradual availability erosion.
recommendation: Use Prometheus recording rules over a 30-day window: `sum_over_time(slo:api_availability:ratio_rate5m[30d])` or integrate with a purpose-built error budget tool (Sloth, Pyrra). At minimum replace the 6h reference with a 30d `avg_over_time`.
acceptance_test_hint: `slo:error_budget_remaining:ratio` decreases monotonically over the course of a simulated 30-day load test with 0.1% error injection; `SLOErrorBudgetLow` fires before the end of the month.

title: Airflow Prometheus scrape uses hardcoded plaintext password `admin`
description: `prometheus.yml:85-87` scrapes Airflow with `basic_auth: username: admin, password: admin`. This is a well-known default credential embedded in a committed config file that Prometheus workers load at runtime. Any operator with read access to this file or the Prometheus config can access the Airflow admin UI. Scope 08 (F-08-009) already flagged plaintext credentials in committed docs; this is an additional instance in infrastructure config.
recommendation: Replace with `password_file: /etc/prometheus/secrets/airflow-password` and provision the secret via Kubernetes Secret or Docker secret, not via the YAML file. At minimum rotate the Airflow admin password and add `prometheus.yml` to `.gitleaks.toml` pattern scanning.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "password:" infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` returns no hits (or returns a file reference, not a value); gitleaks scan of this file returns clean.

title: `gc_collections` Counter incremented with current GC count on every cycle — monotonicity violated
description: Lines 310-311: `for i, count in enumerate(gc.get_count()): gc_collections.labels(generation=str(i)).inc(count)`. `gc.get_count()` returns the current number of collections since the **last** `gc.collect()` call, not since program start. On each 10-second collection loop, this increments the counter by a small number (typically 0-10), not the true cumulative GC count. The Prometheus `rate()` over this counter will be meaningful on average, but `gc.get_count()` does not reset between calls, so values are not deltas — they represent a rolling window internal to CPython's GC. The correct approach is to use `gc.get_stats()` which returns per-generation collection counts since program start.
recommendation: Replace `gc.get_count()` with `gc.get_stats()` which returns a list of dicts with `'collected'` key representing cumulative total. Use `gc_collections.labels(generation=str(i))._value.set(stats['collected'])` with a Gauge, or track the delta manually.
acceptance_test_hint: `rate(gc_collections_total[5m])` in Prometheus returns a smooth non-spiky value during a GC-heavy workload; no counter resets visible in metrics.

title: Duplicate and divergent prometheus.yml in `config/monitoring/` — older stale copy
description: `config/monitoring/prometheus.yml` (57 lines) and `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` (86 lines) are both present and differ significantly: different `external_labels`, missing `rule_files` section in the config copy, missing Nginx/Celery/Airflow scrape jobs, different job names (`backend` vs `investment-api`), different `metrics_path` for the backend (`/metrics` vs `/api/metrics`). The `config/monitoring/` copy appears to be an earlier draft never removed. Two authoritative Prometheus configs cause confusion about which is deployed.
recommendation: Delete `config/monitoring/prometheus.yml`. The `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` is the canonical config (has SLO rule references, complete scrape targets). Verify `docker-compose.yml` mounts `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml` as the active config.
acceptance_test_hint: `find . -name "prometheus.yml" -not -path "*/infrastructure/monitoring/*"` returns no hits; docker-compose volume mount references `infrastructure/monitoring/prometheus.yml`.

title: `on_event("startup"/"shutdown")` deprecated FastAPI lifecycle hooks
description: `metrics_collector.py:675` uses `@app.on_event("startup")` and `@app.on_event("shutdown")`. These decorators were deprecated in FastAPI 0.93 (released 2023-02) and removed in FastAPI 0.110+. The recommended pattern is `lifespan` context manager. If the application runs FastAPI >= 0.110, metrics collection never starts and never stops cleanly.
recommendation: Replace with a `lifespan` async context manager: `from contextlib import asynccontextmanager; @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app): await metrics_collector.start_collection(); yield; await metrics_collector.stop_collection()` and pass to `FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "on_event" backend/monitoring/metrics_collector.py` returns no hits; metrics collection starts on app startup (confirmed via log line "Started metrics collection").

title: Duplicate `HealthStatus` enum defined in `health_checks.py` and `health_system.py`
description: `health_checks.py:28` and `health_system.py:24` both define `class HealthStatus(Enum)` with identical values (`HEALTHY`, `DEGRADED`, `UNHEALTHY`, `CRITICAL`). Because they are separate enum classes, `HealthStatus.HEALTHY is health_system.HealthStatus.HEALTHY` is `False`. Any code that imports from one module and compares with a value from the other will fail equality checks silently. `__init__.py` uses `health_checks.setup_health_monitoring` while `health_system` is also imported independently.
recommendation: Delete `health_system.HealthStatus` and import it from `health_checks` (or move to a shared `backend/monitoring/types.py`). Ensure all references in `health_system.py` use the imported type.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "class HealthStatus" backend/monitoring/` returns exactly 1 hit; `isinstance(health_system.ServiceHealth(...).status, health_checks.HealthStatus)` is `True`.

title: `sla_tracker` uses `get_redis()` which is subject to the fail-open vulnerability (F-08-008)
description: `sla_tracker.py:16` imports `from backend.utils.cache import get_redis`; line 224 sets `self.redis = await get_redis()`. The auth scope audit (F-08-008) found that `redis_resilience.py` fails open — when Redis is unavailable, it returns a no-op client instead of raising. In `sla_tracker.py`, if Redis is in fail-open mode, SLA measurements silently succeed (`redis.set()` returns `True`) but are written to a no-op sink. SLA compliance records appear normal while actually empty.
recommendation: Add a Redis connectivity check before recording SLA measurements: verify `self.redis` is not the fail-open stub before `redis.set()`. At minimum log a warning when Redis is in fail-open mode. Cross-reference scope 08 fix for the underlying fail-open issue.
acceptance_test_hint: `sla_tracker` raises `SLAStorageUnavailableError` (or logs a warning) when Redis is in fail-open mode; SLA measurements are not silently discarded.

title: `mttr` and `mtbf` Gauges defined but never populated in collection loop
description: `mttr = Gauge('mttr_minutes', ...)` and `mtbf = Gauge('mtbf_hours', ...)` are defined at module level (lines 203-204). The `update_mttr_mtbf()` method exists (line 651) but `grep -rn "update_mttr_mtbf" backend/` shows it is called only from tests, never from application code, incident handlers, or the collection loop. Both gauges always export the default value of 0, making the `mttr_minutes` and `mtbf_hours` time-series useless in Grafana.
recommendation: Either: (a) wire `update_mttr_mtbf()` to an incident resolution event (e.g., from `alerting_system.py` when an alert resolves), computing MTTR from `alert.created_at` to resolution time; or (b) remove the gauges until an incident management workflow exists.
acceptance_test_hint: `mttr_minutes{service="database"}` in Prometheus shows non-zero values after simulating a health-check failure and recovery cycle.

title: Dev Prometheus config scrapes backend at `/api/metrics` but endpoint is `/metrics`
description: `prometheus.yml:30` sets `metrics_path: /api/metrics` for the `investment-api` job. `metrics_collector.py:669` registers `@app.get("/metrics")`. The correct scrape path is `/metrics`, not `/api/metrics`. In development, Prometheus will receive 404 responses for every scrape of the backend, producing `up{job="investment-api"} == 0` and triggering the `ServiceDown` alert continuously.
recommendation: Change `prometheus.yml:30` from `metrics_path: /api/metrics` to `metrics_path: /metrics`. (The prod config already has the correct path at `prometheus.prod.yml:43`.)
acceptance_test_hint: `prometheus.yml` scrape config for `investment-api` has `metrics_path: /metrics`; Prometheus target page shows `investment-api` as UP.

title: `sla_compliance` Gauge label set differs between served custom registry and default registry instance

The two definitions use different label sets for the same metric name. If F-10-001 is fixed by unifying to one registry, this will cause a Prometheus duplicate registration error at startup.
recommendation: Consolidate to a single definition with the richer label set `['service', 'sla_type', 'time_window']` in one shared location. Remove the duplicate from whichever module is not the canonical owner.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "sla_compliance_percent" backend/monitoring/` returns exactly 1 definition; Prometheus startup logs show no `duplicate metrics collector registration` error.

title: Test suite queries `/api/health/metrics` but the metrics endpoint is `/metrics`

If no such route exists, every test in `TestMetricsEndpoint` passes a 404 response without asserting the correct status code (tests would need to be checked for assertion strength).
recommendation: Update all test assertions to call `/metrics` instead of `/api/health/metrics`, and add an explicit `assert response.status_code == 200` at the start of each test.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_monitoring_api.py::TestMetricsEndpoint` exits 0 with all assertions against `response.status_code == 200`.

title: Elasticsearch setup code executes on every instantiation despite being permanently disabled
description: `log_analysis.py:585-601` `_setup_elasticsearch()` is called in `__init__`. Even though Elasticsearch is optional and the import is guarded at lines 26-30, the setup method still checks `AsyncElasticsearch is not None` and reads env vars on every `LogAnalysisSystem()` construction. This is dead execution — the env var `ELASTICSEARCH_URL` is never set (Elasticsearch was removed to save $15-20/month per PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATION.md). 20+ lines of dead setup code run pointlessly.
recommendation: Remove `_setup_elasticsearch()` and its call from `__init__`, or guard the entire method behind an explicit `ENABLE_ELASTICSEARCH=true` feature flag that defaults off.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "_setup_elasticsearch\ | elasticsearch_client" backend/monitoring/log_analysis.py` returns 0 hits (after cleanup).

title: Frontend API base paths omit `/v1` — all 40+ endpoints yield 404
description: All `apiConfig.endpoints.*` paths use `/api/auth/login`, `/api/stocks`, etc. Backend registers ALL routers under `/api/v1/` prefix (`main.py:333-348`). The Vite dev proxy rewrites `/api/` to backend but does not insert `/v1/`. Every non-thesis API call is 404 in all envs.
recommendation: Add `v1` segment to all paths in `api.config.ts` (e.g. `/api/v1/auth/login`) OR configure Vite proxy to rewrite `/api/` to `/api/v1/` at the proxy level. Prefer explicit paths.

title: Login thunk reads `response.data.token` but backend field is `access_token`
description: `appSlice.ts:68` — `localStorage.setItem('access_token', response.data.token)`. Backend `Token` schema at `auth.py:44` defines `access_token: str`. ApiResponse wraps it as `{ success, data: { access_token } }`. Frontend reads `response.data.token` — evaluates to `undefined`. Every login stores `undefined` as the auth token; all subsequent requests send `Bearer undefined`.
recommendation: Change line 68 to `localStorage.setItem('access_token', response.data.data?.access_token)` — or update the login thunk to destructure `{ data: { access_token } } = response`. Also log a warning if the value is undefined before storing.
acceptance_test_hint: `appSlice` login thunk test: mock response with `{ data: { access_token: 'tok' } }` and assert `localStorage.getItem('access_token') === 'tok'`

title: No CSP meta tag and Vite build uses eval-adjacent features
description: `index.html` has no Content-Security-Policy meta tag. Vite's React plugin in dev uses `eval` for HMR. Production build uses Terser (safe) but no CSP is set at the HTML layer. Scope 08 audit F-08-003 found backend CSP hardcodes `unsafe-inline unsafe-eval` — the frontend does not add a compensating stricter CSP at the HTML level either. Any XSS in the app has no CSP mitigation.
recommendation: Add `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` to `index.html` with `script-src 'self'`; use nonces for any inline scripts. Remove `unsafe-eval` from nginx/backend CSP (scope 08 F-08-003 fix). Configure Vite to emit nonce-based CSP header.
acceptance_test_hint: Lighthouse security audit shows CSP present; browser DevTools shows no CSP violation on page load

title: Root-level CorrelationMatrix/EfficientFrontier/RiskDecomposition are dead duplicate code

Only the `portfolio/` versions are imported (from `PortfolioChart.tsx:14-16`). Root-level copies are dead code bundled into the vendor chunk increasing build output.

acceptance_test_hint: `vite build` completes with no import errors; bundle size decreases by ~3 deduplicated chunks

title: InvestmentThesis bypasses central API service — raw axios, hardcoded URL, manual token

Remove raw axios import and localStorage calls. | All thesis CRUD operations work in integration; token refresh on 401 is exercised automatically

title: PortfolioMetrics interface missing analytics fields — escaped with `as any`
description: `PortfolioMetrics` interface does not declare `correlationMatrix`, `efficientFrontier`, or `diversificationScore`. `PortfolioChart.tsx:102` uses `(metrics as any)?.correlationMatrix`, line 110 `(metrics as any)?.efficientFrontier?.points`, line 112 `(metrics as any)?.efficientFrontier?.optimalPosition`. `Portfolio.tsx:443` uses `(metrics as any)?.diversificationScore`. These `as any` casts silently hide schema drift if the backend changes field names.
recommendation: Extend `PortfolioMetrics` in `portfolioSlice.ts` with optional typed fields: `correlationMatrix?: Record<string, number>; efficientFrontier?: { points: {risk: number; return: number}[]; currentPosition: {risk: number; return: number}; optimalPosition?: {risk: number; return: number} }; diversificationScore?: number`. Remove all `as any` casts.

title: Three dead production dependencies: `react-beautiful-dnd`, `plotly.js`, `react-plotly.js`
description: `grep -rn "react-beautiful-dnd" src` — 0 results. `grep -rn "from 'plotly" src` — 0 results. `grep -rn "from 'react-plotly" src` — 0 results. Yet `package.json` lists all three as production `dependencies`. Plotly alone is ~2.8MB minified; it inflates `npm install` time and may be included in vendor chunks if the manualChunks guard is encountered unexpectedly.
recommendation: Remove `react-beautiful-dnd`, `@types/react-beautiful-dnd`, `plotly.js`, `react-plotly.js`, `@types/react-plotly.js` from package.json. Run `npm install` then `npm run build` to verify no broken imports.

title: Catch-block uses `err: any` and leaks raw API error detail to UI
description: `InvestmentThesis.tsx:169` — `catch (err: any) { setError(err.response?.data?.detail \
acceptance_test_hint: 'Failed…') }`. Displaying `err.response?.data?.detail` verbatim can leak internal server error messages, stack traces, or database field names to the user. This is an XSS-adjacent pattern if the backend ever returns user-controlled content in `detail`. | Replace `err: any` with `err: unknown`. Use a typed error handler: `const message = isAxiosError(err) && err.response?.status !== 500 ? err.response?.data?.detail : 'An error occurred'`. Never display 500-level detail to users. | Unit test: mock a 500 response with `detail: 'SQL error: ...'` and assert the displayed message is the generic fallback string

title: WebSocket subscribes to `state.portfolio.watchlist?.items` — property path not in PortfolioState
description: `websocket.service.ts:144` — `state.portfolio.watchlist?.items`. Looking at `portfolioSlice.ts`, the state structure contains `watchlists: Watchlist[]` and `selectedWatchlist: Watchlist
recommendation: null` but no `.watchlist.items` direct path. This access silently returns `undefined`, so watchlist stock subscriptions are never sent to the server — no real-time price updates for watchlisted items.

Add an integration test for `subscribeToChannels`. | Manual test: add a stock to watchlist, observe WebSocket `subscribe` emit in browser DevTools Network

title: ErrorBoundary uses `process.env.NODE_ENV` — unreliable in Vite production
description: `ErrorBoundary.tsx:38` — `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production')`. Vite replaces `import.meta.env.MODE` not `process.env.NODE_ENV`. In a Vite build, `process.env.NODE_ENV` may or may not be injected depending on the plugin config. If it evaluates falsy in production, the error detail block renders for all users, leaking stack traces.
recommendation: Replace `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` with `import.meta.env.PROD` (Vite's canonical boolean). Also replace the duplicate `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` guard at line 99.
acceptance_test_hint: `npm run build` and serve; trigger an error in the built app; confirm error detail block is NOT rendered

title: Login thunk stores `response.data.token` but refresh interceptor stores `response.data.access_token`
description: Login path: `appSlice.ts:68` sets `localStorage.setItem('access_token', response.data.token)`. Refresh path in `api.service.ts:57-58`: `const { access_token } = response.data; localStorage.setItem('access_token', access_token)`. Even if fixed for the backend response structure, these two code paths use different destructuring patterns and must remain in sync.
recommendation: Centralise token persistence in a `tokenStorage.ts` utility (`setAccessToken`, `getAccessToken`, `clearTokens`) used by both `appSlice.ts` and `api.service.ts`. This eliminates the sync problem.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit tests for `tokenStorage` module; both login and refresh paths call the same setter

title: `stock:trade` event handler delegates to unimplemented `handleTradeUpdate`
description: `websocket.service.ts:81-84` — `this.socket.on('stock:trade', (data) => { this.handleTradeUpdate(data); })`. No `handleTradeUpdate` method is defined in the class. TypeScript strict mode does not catch this because it appears to be callable but `this.handleTradeUpdate` will throw `TypeError: this.handleTradeUpdate is not a function` at runtime on every trade event.
recommendation: Implement `handleTradeUpdate(data: unknown): void` or replace with an inline dispatch. Add a `TradeUpdate` interface.
acceptance_test_hint: `websocket.service.ts` compiles without error; unit test: mock socket, emit `stock:trade`, verify no TypeError

title: Route prefetch `setTimeout` leaks memory if component unmounts before timeout fires
description: `App.tsx:96-103` — `const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => { routesToPrefetch.forEach(prefetchRoute); }, 1000); return () => clearTimeout(timeoutId)`. The cleanup is correct. However `prefetchRoute` calls `routeModules[route]()` which triggers a dynamic import — if the import resolves after the component has unmounted, React will log a state update on unmounted component warning. The imported modules are side-effect free so this is low risk, but the pattern is not idiomatic.
recommendation: The existing `clearTimeout` cleanup is correct. No urgent fix needed. Consider replacing with `requestIdleCallback` for non-essential prefetching to avoid competing with visible page resources.
acceptance_test_hint: No "Can't perform state update on unmounted component" warnings in console after rapid navigation

title: No test coverage for `api.service.ts`, `websocket.service.ts`, or `api.config.ts` — core integration layer
description: `find src -name "*.test.*"` — no test file for `services/api.service.ts`, `services/websocket.service.ts`, `config/api.config.ts`. These files implement the auth interceptor, token refresh, WebSocket reconnection — the most business-critical client logic. With the schema mismatches found (F-12-001, F-12-002), tests would have caught these issues.

acceptance_test_hint: `npm run test:coverage` shows api.service.ts and websocket.service.ts at >80% branch coverage

No cache TTL, no deduplication, no automatic refetch on focus. With 40+ endpoints, the boilerplate volume is high and inconsistent (some slices have `isLoading`, others use `status`).

description: `SearchModal:67` — `localStorage.getItem('recentSearches')`, `SearchModal:105` — `localStorage.setItem('recentSearches', JSON.stringify(updated))`. No max age, no cap on number of entries (no limit on the `updated` array). Over time this can grow large.

title: `.env*` baked into image
description: `COPY .env* ./` copies any `.env`, `.env.production`, `.env.staging` into the image layer. Same in Dockerfile.ml-monitoring:20 and Dockerfile.ml-scheduler:21. .dockerignore excludes plain `.env` and `.env.*` but re-includes `!.env.example` / `!.env.*.example` only — names like `.env.production` should be ignored, but tightness depends on docker resolving negation precedence; one stray `.env.local` baked in image is a credential leak.

title: CNAME records point to placeholder + invalid target type

title: Source bind-mounts in base compose leak into production
description: Base `docker-compose.yml` (which `production.yml` extends) mounts `./backend:/app/backend` and `./frontend/web:/app`. The production overlay does not declare `volumes: []` reset, so production containers run host source code instead of the immutable image — defeats reproducibility, breaks read-only filesystems, complicates rollback.
recommendation: In docker-compose.production.yml, explicitly set `volumes:` for backend/frontend services to only the runtime mounts (logs, models:ro, data) and either remove dev mounts from base compose or split bases so prod doesn't inherit them.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml config | grep -A3 'backend:' | grep -q './backend:/app/backend'` returns nothing

title: nginx prod healthcheck hits `/nginx_status` only allowed from internal IPs
description: Healthcheck `curl -f http://localhost/nginx_status` runs inside the container; localhost matches `allow 127.0.0.1` so it works at runtime. But `/nginx_status` is only defined inside the **HTTP** server block in nginx.optimized.conf:282-290 — the **HTTPS** server (line 93) does not define it. If the healthcheck is bound to 443 only (TLS), it will return 404. Conflict with `/health` endpoint that IS defined on both servers (lines 180,275).
recommendation: Change healthcheck to `curl -f http://localhost/health` for parity with infrastructure/docker/nginx/nginx.conf:55 and nginx-ssl.conf:113.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -fs http://localhost/health` inside container returns 200

title: `ssl_dhparam` and `ssl_trusted_certificate` reference files not in repo
description: nginx-ssl.conf requires `/etc/nginx/ssl/dhparam.pem` and `/etc/nginx/ssl/chain.pem`. `ssl/` directory contains only `.gitkeep`. Production startup will fail with `cannot load certificate "/etc/nginx/ssl/dhparam.pem"`.
recommendation: Generate dhparam at deploy time (compose init container or Makefile target) and document that chain.pem must come from Let's Encrypt; OR remove `ssl_dhparam` and `ssl_trusted_certificate` directives if not strictly required.
acceptance_test_hint: `nginx -t` inside investment_nginx_prod returns "test is successful" with provisioned certs

title: TA-Lib downloaded via insecure `http://prdownloads.sourceforge.net`
description: Plain HTTP download; redirect chain susceptible to MITM, breaks reproducibility. infrastructure/docker/backend/Dockerfile uses `https://github.com/ta-lib/ta-lib/releases/...` — preferred.
recommendation: Use the GitHub URL; pin to a specific tag/sha; verify checksum.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n 'http://prdownloads' Dockerfile.backend` returns 0 hits

Network during build is fragile, ties build to HuggingFace availability, increases image size by ~500MB+. Also references `backend/ml/models/` for `COPY` — directory may not exist (broken_dependency in some checkouts).

title: Embedded `RUN echo 'server {...}'` overwrites the prior COPY of nginx.conf
description: Lines 45-46 COPY `nginx.conf` and `security-headers.conf`, then lines 49-66 echo a literal default.conf that overrides defaults — dual-config pattern is fragile and config drift between embedded server block and the COPYed conf is high.
recommendation: Drop the inline echo; rely solely on the COPYed configs. Keep one source of truth.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker run <frontend> cat /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` shows no embedded `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;` if removed

title: Duplicate HTTP and HTTPS server blocks with full app routing
description: Both port 80 and 443 server blocks define `location /`, `/api/`, `/ws`, etc. Port 80 should only do ACME + redirect (per nginx-ssl.conf which does this correctly). Current optimized.conf serves the app over plain HTTP.
recommendation: Reduce HTTP server to ACME challenge + 301 redirect to HTTPS; remove duplicated app routes from port 80.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI http://host/` returns `HTTP/1.1 301` Location: https

title: `location` blocks inside an included security-headers file
description: nginx `include` of a file containing `location {}` directives is only valid when included inside a server block. The same file is included in nginx.optimized.conf:115 *inside* server{}, fine, but in nginx-ssl.conf:110 also inside server{} — works. However the conf-mode duplication (security-headers.conf in nginx/conf.d auto-loaded vs security-headers.conf in frontend/) creates two divergent files. The frontend variant has location blocks; the nginx variant does not. This means `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` is enforced on the frontend SPA — will break embedded third-party widgets unless explicitly opted in.
recommendation: Consolidate into one canonical security-headers.conf. Reconsider COEP=require-corp for SPA — typically `unsafe-none` or `credentialless` is safer for apps that load any cross-origin resources.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI https://host/ | grep -i cross-origin-embedder` returns desired value

title: CSP allows `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts
description: `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' ...`. Defeats CSP's main purpose against XSS. The frontend variant (security-headers.conf in frontend/) does NOT include these — divergence.
recommendation: Remove `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` from script-src; use nonces or hashes for any required inline.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI https://host/ | grep -i content-security | grep -v "'unsafe-eval'"` returns the header

title: Base compose missing `version:` directive while production.yml:5 still has `version: '3.8'`
description: Inconsistent: base file omits version key (modern Compose Spec), but production/test/ml-production overlays declare `version: '3.8'` (legacy). Mixing causes deprecation warnings and may load different schemas.
recommendation: Either remove `version:` from all compose files (modern) or set consistently. Modern Docker Compose (>=2.0) ignores it but warns.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml config 2>&1 | grep -i 'version is obsolete'` returns 0

title: nginx service in base compose duplicates production nginx
description: Base `docker-compose.yml` defines an nginx reverse proxy at port 80/443 mounting `infrastructure/docker/nginx/nginx.conf`. Production overlay defines another nginx (line 274) mounting `infrastructure/docker/frontend/nginx.optimized.conf`. Two nginx configs, two paths, hard to reason about.
recommendation: Delete nginx from base compose; let dev use frontend container's embedded nginx. Production overlay owns the load balancer.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config | grep -c 'image: nginx'` is 0 in dev, 1 in prod

title: dev frontend env points to `localhost:8000` but maps port 3000
description: `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8000` is a build-time arg in the production Dockerfile but a runtime env in dev compose. Vite only reads `VITE_*` at build time; setting at runtime in dev (line 139) has no effect on a built bundle. Works only because dev compose runs `npm start` (Vite dev server) which does pick up env. Confusing for prod — but in production.yml it is correctly passed as `args:`.
recommendation: Document or move VITE_* into `args` for any built target; clarify in compose comments which mode each block targets.
acceptance_test_hint: comment block at top of docker-compose.yml lists VITE behavior

title: Hard-coded `python3.12` site-packages path
description: `PYTHONPATH=/app:/home/appuser/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` — coupled to PYTHON_VERSION ARG (3.12). If ARG changes, path drifts silently.
recommendation: Use `python -c "import site; print(site.USER_SITE)"` at build time, or rely on PATH+sys.path defaults instead of hard-coding.
acceptance_test_hint: bumping PYTHON_VERSION ARG to 3.13 still resolves imports

title: `npm ci --only=production` then trying to run `npm run build`
description: `--only=production` skips devDependencies; Vite, TypeScript, and most build toolchains live in devDependencies. Build typically fails unless those moved to dependencies. infrastructure/docker/frontend/Dockerfile uses `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` (broader).
recommendation: Use `npm ci` (no `--only=production`) in builder stage; production-only install belongs only in serving stage which here is nginx (no Node).
acceptance_test_hint: `docker build -f Dockerfile.frontend .` succeeds without missing-vite errors

title: `.dockerignore` excludes `Dockerfile*` and `docker-compose*.yml`
description: Excluding all `Dockerfile*` is fine since they aren't COPYed, but excluding `docker-compose*.yml` then having ml Dockerfiles `COPY .env* ./` is moot — but the broader concern is that `!.env.example` exception only un-ignores literal `.env.example`. Patterns like `.env.production.example` (allowed by `!.env.*.example`) are intended for shipping templates; current rule pair is correct. Marking as low after re-verification.
recommendation: No change required; document the negation rules with a comment so future edits don't break them.
acceptance_test_hint: n/a

title: Script injection via untrusted issue title/body
description: `TITLE="${{ github.event.issue.title }}"` and `BODY="${{ github.event.issue.body }}"` inlined into shell on a `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` job. An attacker filing an issue with a backtick/`$()` payload in the title can execute arbitrary code in CI with the workflow token.
recommendation: Pass user-controlled fields via `env:` and reference as `"$TITLE"` inside `run:`; never interpolate `${{ github.event.* }}` directly into shell.
acceptance_test_hint: Re-run workflow against a test issue with title `$(echo PWNED)`; verify literal string is logged, not command output.

title: TA-Lib downloaded over plaintext HTTP without checksum
description: `wget http://prdownloads.sourceforge.net/ta-lib/ta-lib-0.4.0-src.tar.gz` runs in 7+ workflows. No HTTPS, no SHA256 verification → trivially MITM'd by any on-path attacker (CI runners egress through public internet). The unpacked source is then `make install`'d as root.
recommendation: Switch to HTTPS, pin to known SHA256, OR build TA-Lib once into a base Docker image consumed via `container:`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -E "wget http://prdownloads" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns 0; new install step has `sha256sum -c`.

title: Third-party actions pinned only to floating major tags
description: `uses: docker/build-push-action@v5`, `8398a7/action-slack@v3`, `dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3`, `appleboy/ssh-action@v1`, `gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2`, `returntocorp/semgrep-action@v1`, `anchore/sbom-action@v0`, `hadolint/hadolint-action@v3`, etc. — `grep -E "uses:.*@[a-f0-9]{40}"` returns 0 hits. A compromised tag (Tj-actions style supply-chain attack) executes immediately on next CI run.
recommendation: Pin every third-party action to a full 40-char commit SHA with a comment indicating the tag, e.g. `uses: docker/build-push-action@4f580a... # v5.3.0`. Configure Dependabot ecosystem `github-actions` (already on per `.github/dependabot.yml:115`) to bump SHAs.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -cE "uses: [^@]+@[a-f0-9]{40}" .github/workflows/*.yml` ≥ count of `uses:` lines for non-`actions/*` and non-`./` references.

title: Two duplicate mypy workflows with conflicting configs
description: `mypy.yml` runs Python 3.11; `type-check.yml` runs Python 3.12, has a 3636-error baseline gate. Triggers overlap (both fire on `backend/**/*.py` PRs to main/develop). Wastes runner minutes and produces conflicting status checks.
recommendation: Keep `type-check.yml` (newer, has baseline gate); delete `mypy.yml`. Or merge into a single workflow with matrix.
acceptance_test_hint: After consolidation, `ls .github/workflows/{mypy,type-check}.yml` shows only one; PR builds run mypy exactly once.

title: Workflows missing top-level `permissions:` block
description: `grep -c "permissions:" .github/workflows/*.yml` shows 0 for these workflows, so they inherit the repo default (often `contents: write` for legacy repos). Violates least-privilege; if a step is compromised it gets write access to repo contents and packages.
recommendation: Add `permissions: contents: read` (or narrower) at workflow top; grant write only on the specific job that needs it.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -L "^permissions:" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns empty (every workflow declares permissions).

title: Mixed CodeQL action versions (`@v2` and `@v3`)
description: `grep github/codeql-action .github/workflows/*.yml` shows `init@v3`, `analyze@v3`, but `upload-sarif@v2` co-exists with `upload-sarif@v3`. v2 is deprecated by GitHub and will be removed; mismatched versions can drop SARIF uploads silently.
recommendation: Standardize on `github/codeql-action/*@v3` everywhere.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "codeql-action.*@v2" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns 0.

recommendation: Reduce matrix to `['3.12']` OR justify with explicit "library-style" reasoning. Move 3.10/3.11 to a nightly-only job.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "python-version: \[" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns single-element list.

recommendation: Either wire `workflow-coordinator.yml` build job to call `reusable-build.yml`, or delete the file.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable-build" .github/` returns ≥1 OR the file no longer exists.

title: OptimizedRecommendationEngine import outside skip guard causes collection failure
description: `pytest.importorskip("objgraph")` at line 15 guards lines 16–33, but line 34 `from backend.analytics.recommendation_engine import OptimizedRecommendationEngine` is outside the try/except. When objgraph is installed, pytest reaches line 34 and the import of `OptimizedRecommendationEngine` triggers `AttributeError` because `_scan_market_optimized` calls `scanner.scan_market_streaming` which does not exist on `MarketScanner` (confirmed by scope 09 F-09-002). All 50+ tests in this file are silently killed at collection time.
recommendation: Move line 34 inside the try block (lines 16–33) or add a separate `try/except ImportError` around it with `pytest.skip`.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest --collect-only backend/tests/test_performance_optimizations.py` returns 50+ test items without errors

title: Jest flags passed to Vitest break frontend CI test run
description: `npm test -- --watchAll=false --passWithNoTests` passes Jest/CRA-specific flags to vitest 4.x. Vitest 4.x does not recognise `--watchAll` or `--passWithNoTests`; unrecognised CLI options cause vitest to exit with a non-zero error code, making the `--frontend` and `--all` modes of `run-tests.sh` fail or silently skip all frontend unit tests. The correct vitest equivalent is `vitest run`.
recommendation: Replace line 84 with: `if npm run test -- --run; then` (vitest recognises `--run` for single-pass CI mode). Remove `--watchAll=false --passWithNoTests`.
acceptance_test_hint: `./run-tests.sh --frontend` exits 0 and shows vitest test results for 16 test files in src/

acceptance_test_hint: `pytest --collect-only tests/` returns test items; `pytest tests/ -q` passes without import errors

title: FinnhubWebSocketClient.connect() session-lifetime bug has no direct test coverage
description: Scope 02 (F-02-002) confirmed that `FinnhubWebSocketClient.connect()` opens `aiohttp.ClientSession` inside `async with`, schedules `_receive_task`, then exits the `async with` block — closing the session immediately on every connect. The test file (`test_realtime_price_service.py`) has `TestFinnhubWebSocketClientInit`, `TestSubscribeUnsubscribe`, `TestHandleConnectionError`, and `TestDisconnect` — but **no `TestConnect` class**. All reconnect tests (`TestHandleConnectionError:547-641`) mock `.connect()` via `patch.object(ws_client, "connect", new_callable=AsyncMock)`, meaning the actual session-lifetime bug is never exercised.
recommendation: Add `TestConnect` class testing `connect()` with a real or minimally-mocked `aiohttp.ClientSession` to verify that the `ws` attribute remains open after the `async with` block exits.

The test therefore cannot catch the production bug. Same pattern in `test_analytics_extended_agent4.py:839-846`.
